questions.topic: Counting in millions, billions and trillions
questions.stem: Write 4,060,000,300 in words.
options: four billion, sixty million, three thousand
four billion, six million, three hundred
four billion, sixty million, three hundred
forty billion, sixty million, three hundred
questions.explanation: 4,060,000,300 has 4 in the billions place, 60 in the millions group and 300 in the units group.

questions.topic: Counting in millions, billions and trillions
questions.stem: How many millions make one trillion?
questions.explanation: One trillion is 1,000,000,000,000 and dividing by 1,000,000 gives 1,000,000 millions.

questions.topic: Counting in millions, billions and trillions
questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 7 in 3,725,410,000?
questions.explanation: The 7 is in the hundred-millions place, so its value is 700,000,000.

questions.stem: Express 3,250,000,000 in standard form.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 9 places to the left to get 3.25, so the number is 3.25 x 10^9.

questions.stem: A state has a population of 15,400,000. Write this in standard form.
Write 2.06 x 10^5 as an ordinary number.
questions.explanation: Multiplying 2.06 by 100,000 moves the decimal point 5 places to the right, giving 206,000.

questions.stem: Express 0.00048 in standard form.
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 4 places to the right to get 4.8, so the power of 10 is -4.

questions.stem: The thickness of a sheet of paper is 0.0095 cm. Write this in standard form.
Evaluate (6 x 10^4) x (3 x 10^-2), giving your answer in standard form.
Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 37 has no factors other than 1 and itself; 39 = 3 x 13, 51 = 3 x 17 and 57 = 3 x 19.

questions.stem: What are the prime factors of 84?
questions.explanation: 84 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 7, so the prime factors are 2, 3 and 7.

questions.stem: Express 360 as a product of its prime factors in index form.

questions.explanation: 2,025 = 3^4 x 5^2, so its square root is 3^2 x 5 = 45.

questions.stem: A square farm plot has an area of 196 m^2. What is the length of one side?
questions.explanation: The side of a square is the square root of its area; the square root of 196 is 14.

questions.stem: What is the smallest whole number by which 72 must be multiplied to give a perfect square?
questions.explanation: 72 = 2^3 x 3^2. One more factor of 2 makes 2^4 x 3^2 = 144, which is 12^2.

questions.stem: The binary number system uses only the digits
questions.explanation: Binary is base two, so its only digits are 0 and 1.

questions.stem: Why do computers use the binary number system?
options: Their electronic switches have only two states, on and off
It uses ten digits like everyday counting
Binary numbers are always shorter than decimal numbers
questions.explanation: A computer circuit is either on (1) or off (0), which matches the two binary digits.

questions.topic: Using the computer for simple calculations
questions.stem: In a spreadsheet, which formula adds the numbers in cells A1 to A5?
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet formulas begin with = and SUM(A1:A5) adds the range A1 to A5.

questions.topic: Using the computer for simple calculations
questions.stem: When using a computer calculator program, the symbol * is used for
questions.explanation: On computers the asterisk * means multiply and / means divide.

questions.topic: Translating word problems into numerical expressions
questions.stem: Ada bought 3 exercise books at ₦450 each and 2 biros at ₦120 each. Which expression gives the total cost?
questions.explanation: Cost of books is 3 x 450 and cost of biros is 2 x 120; add them.

questions.topic: Translating word problems into numerical expressions
questions.stem: Musa had ₦5,000. He bought 3 loaves of bread at ₦1,250 each. How much did he have left?
Simplify 3/4 x (2/3 + 1/6).
If 12 workers can build a fence in 15 days, how many days will 9 workers take, working at the same rate?
questions.explanation: This is inverse proportion: 12 x 15 = 180 worker-days, and 180 ÷ 9 = 20 days.

questions.stem: 4 tins of milk cost ₦2,400. What is the cost of 7 tins?
questions.explanation: One tin costs 2,400 ÷ 4 = ₦600, so 7 tins cost 7 x 600 = ₦4,200.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of inverse proportion?
options: The number of oranges bought and their total cost
The distance covered and the time taken at a steady speed
The number of people sharing a cake and the size of each share
The number of hours worked and the wages earned at a fixed rate
questions.explanation: When more people share a cake, each share becomes smaller, so one quantity rises as the other falls.

questions.topic: Application of direct and inverse proportions
questions.stem: A car travelling at 60 km/h takes 3 hours for a journey. How long will it take at 80 km/h?
questions.explanation: Distance = 60 x 3 = 180 km; time = 180 ÷ 80 = 2.25 hours = 2 1/4 hours.

questions.topic: Application of direct and inverse proportions
questions.stem: Food in a school store lasts 60 boarders for 25 days. If 15 more boarders arrive, how long will the food last?
questions.explanation: 60 x 25 = 1,500 boarder-days; 1,500 ÷ 75 = 20 days.

questions.stem: Find the simple interest on ₦50,000 for 3 years at 8% per annum.
Chika saved ₦80,000 in a bank that pays 5% simple interest per annum. What will be the total amount after 2 years?
At what rate per annum will ₦40,000 earn ₦6,000 simple interest in 3 years?
Find the amount after 2 years if ₦20,000 is invested at 10% compound interest per annum.
What is the compound interest on ₦100,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum?
Find the LCM of 12, 18 and 30.
Three bells ring at intervals of 15, 20 and 25 minutes. If they ring together at 8:00 a.m., when will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: LCM of 15, 20 and 25 is 300 minutes = 5 hours, so 8:00 a.m. + 5 hours = 1:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: The greatest equal length is the HCF of 84 and 126, which is 42 m.

questions.stem: Find the HCF of 2^3 x 3^2 x 5 and 2^2 x 3^3 x 7.
questions.explanation: Take the lowest power of each common prime: 2^2 and 3^2.

questions.stem: Which of these fractions is equivalent to 3/5?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the numerator and denominator of 3/5 by 4 gives 12/20.

questions.stem: Find the missing number: 4/7 = ?/56
questions.explanation: 56 ÷ 7 = 8, so the numerator is 4 x 8 = 32.

questions.stem: In a class of 40 pupils, 3/8 are boys. How many girls are in the class?
Arrange 2/3, 5/8 and 3/4 in ascending order.
Which is the largest of 4/9, 3/7, 5/11 and 1/2?
questions.explanation: Each of the other fractions is less than half of its denominator, so 1/2 is the largest.

questions.topic: Expressing fractions as ratios, decimals and percentages
questions.stem: Tolu spent 3/10 of her pocket money on snacks. Which of these does NOT represent the same part?
questions.explanation: 3/10 = 0.3 = 30%, and as a ratio of part to whole it is 3 : 10. 3 : 7 compares the part spent with the part left, not with the whole.

questions.topic: Quantitative reasoning on fractions and ratios
questions.stem: ₦36,000 is shared between Emeka and Bola in the ratio 2 : 7. How much does Emeka get?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 9; Emeka gets 2/9 x 36,000 = ₦8,000.

questions.topic: Quantitative reasoning on fractions and ratios
questions.stem: The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 5 : 3. If there are 24 girls, how many members are in the club?
questions.explanation: 3 parts = 24 so 1 part = 8; total = 8 parts = 64.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-rational (irrational) number?
questions.explanation: The square root of 5 cannot be written as a fraction of two whole numbers; the square root of 16 is 4.

questions.stem: A rational number is a number that can be written in the form
options: a + b, where a and b are whole numbers
a/b, where a and b are integers and b is not zero
a decimal that never ends and never repeats
questions.explanation: Rational numbers are ratios of integers with a non-zero denominator.

questions.stem: Which statement about pi is correct?
options: It is irrational; 22/7 and 3.14 are only approximations to it
It is a rational number equal to 3.14
questions.explanation: Pi has a decimal that never ends or repeats, so it is irrational.

questions.stem: Express 0.333... (3 recurring) as a fraction.
questions.explanation: Let x = 0.333...; 10x = 3.333...; subtracting gives 9x = 3, so x = 1/3.

questions.explanation: A 14-year-old usually weighs between about 40 kg and 60 kg.

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of the capacity of a standard bucket used at home?
questions.explanation: A household bucket holds roughly 10 litres of water.

questions.stem: A pupil walks to school in about 15 minutes at a normal pace. Which is the best estimate of the distance?
questions.explanation: People walk about 4 to 5 km in an hour, so 15 minutes is roughly 1 km.

questions.stem: By rounding each number to the nearest ten, estimate 48 x 21.
questions.explanation: 48 is about 50 and 21 is about 20; 50 x 20 = 1,000.

questions.topic: Approximating results of addition and subtraction
questions.stem: Estimate 3,912 + 6,087 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand.
questions.explanation: 3,912 is about 4,000 and 6,087 is about 6,000, so the estimate is 10,000.

questions.topic: Approximating results of multiplication and division
questions.stem: By rounding each number to 1 significant figure, estimate 612 ÷ 29.
questions.explanation: 612 is about 600 and 29 is about 30; 600 ÷ 30 = 20.

questions.topic: Rounding off to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000
questions.stem: Round 47,650 to the nearest thousand.
questions.explanation: The hundreds digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 48,000.

questions.topic: Rounding off to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000
questions.stem: Round 3,048 to the nearest hundred.
questions.explanation: The tens digit is 4, which is less than 5, so round down to 3,000.

questions.topic: Application of approximation in everyday life
questions.stem: A crate of soft drinks costs ₦4,850. Approximately how much will 9 crates cost, to the nearest thousand naira?
questions.explanation: 9 x 4,850 = ₦43,650, which is ₦44,000 to the nearest thousand.

questions.stem: Express 0.004726 correct to 2 significant figures.
questions.explanation: The first two significant figures are 4 and 7; the next digit, 2, is less than 5, so 0.0047.

questions.stem: Write 18.4769 correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: The third decimal digit is 6, so the second decimal place 7 rounds up to 8.

questions.stem: Write 52,749 correct to 3 significant figures.
questions.explanation: The first three significant figures are 527; the next digit, 4, is less than 5, and zeros keep the place value.

questions.stem: The length of a rod is given as 6.4 m, correct to 1 decimal place. What is the least possible length of the rod?
questions.explanation: Any length from 6.35 m up to (but not including) 6.45 m rounds to 6.4 m, so the least is 6.35 m.

questions.explanation: Selling price = 120% of cost, so cost = 36,000 ÷ 1.2 = ₦30,000.

questions.explanation: From 07:45 to 10:00 is 2 h 15 min, plus 20 min gives 2 h 35 min.

questions.topic: Similarities and differences between plane shapes
questions.stem: Which property does a rhombus have that a general parallelogram does NOT have?
questions.explanation: Every parallelogram has the other three properties; only a rhombus must have four equal sides.

questions.topic: Similarities and differences between plane shapes
questions.stem: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is called a
questions.explanation: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides.

questions.topic: Similarities and differences between plane shapes
questions.stem: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square has two diagonal and two middle lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: Find the perimeter of a rectangle 14 cm long and 9 cm wide.
Find the circumference of a circle of radius 21 cm. (Take pi = 22/7)
questions.explanation: C = 2 x pi x r = 2 x 22/7 x 21 = 132 cm.

questions.stem: A square garden has a perimeter of 60 m. What is its area?
A rectangular plot is 50 m by 30 m. Fencing costs ₦400 per metre. What is the cost of fencing the plot?
Find the area of a rectangle measuring 12 m by 7.5 m.
questions.explanation: Area = length x breadth = 12 x 7.5 = 90 m^2.

questions.stem: A triangle with sides 2 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm is enlarged by a scale factor of 3. What is the longest side of the image?
questions.explanation: Each side is multiplied by 3, so 4 cm becomes 12 cm.

questions.stem: On a map with scale 1 : 50,000, two towns are 6 cm apart. What is the actual distance between them?

questions.topic: Lengths, areas and volumes of similar figures
questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 2 : 5. What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: The ratio of areas of similar figures is the square of the ratio of lengths: 2^2 : 5^2 = 4 : 25.

questions.topic: Lengths, areas and volumes of similar figures
questions.stem: Two similar tins have heights 6 cm and 12 cm. If the smaller tin holds 250 ml, how much does the larger tin hold?
questions.explanation: Length ratio 1 : 2 gives volume ratio 1 : 8, so 250 x 8 = 2,000 ml.

questions.stem: How many edges does a cuboid have?
questions.explanation: A cuboid has 6 faces, 8 vertices and 12 edges.

questions.stem: How many vertices (corners) does a cube have?
questions.explanation: A cube has 8 vertices.

questions.stem: A square-based pyramid has how many faces?
questions.explanation: It has 1 square base and 4 triangular faces, giving 5 faces.

questions.stem: Which solid has one flat circular face, one curved surface and a vertex?
questions.explanation: A cone has a circular base, a curved surface and a vertex.

questions.stem: Which of these objects is shaped like a cylinder?
questions.explanation: A tin has two equal circular ends and a curved side, like a cylinder.

questions.stem: How many flat faces does a sphere have?
questions.explanation: A sphere has only one curved surface and no flat faces.

questions.stem: Find the volume of a cuboid 8 cm long, 5 cm wide and 3 cm high.
questions.explanation: V = l x b x h = 8 x 5 x 3 = 120 cm^3.

questions.stem: The volume of a cube is 216 cm^3. What is the length of one edge?
questions.explanation: Edge = cube root of 216 = 6 cm because 6 x 6 x 6 = 216.

questions.stem: A water tank in the shape of a cuboid measures 2 m by 1.5 m by 1 m. How many litres can it hold? (1 m^3 = 1,000 litres)
questions.explanation: Volume = 2 x 1.5 x 1 = 3 m^3 = 3,000 litres.

questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines meet at 90°.

questions.stem: When a line segment AB is bisected with ruler and compasses, the bisector
options: cuts AB into two equal parts at right angles
questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisector meets AB at 90° at its midpoint.

questions.stem: To construct an angle of 30° with ruler and compasses, you first construct
options: an angle of 90° and then bisect it
an angle of 60° and then bisect it
an angle of 45° and then bisect it
an angle of 120° and then trisect it
questions.explanation: Bisecting a 60° angle gives two 30° angles.

questions.stem: Which angle is obtained by bisecting a constructed right angle?
questions.explanation: Half of 90° is 45°.

questions.stem: Which set of lengths can form a triangle?
questions.explanation: In a triangle any two sides must add up to more than the third: 5 + 7 = 12 > 10.

questions.stem: The bisector of an angle
options: divides the angle in the ratio 1 : 2
divides the angle into two equal angles
questions.explanation: To bisect means to cut into two equal parts.

questions.stem: When copying a given angle with ruler and compasses, which instrument transfers the opening between the arms?
questions.explanation: The compasses measure the arc distance between the arms and transfer it to the new angle.

questions.stem: To construct a square of side 5 cm with ruler and compasses, which angle must be constructed at the corners?
questions.explanation: Every angle of a square is a right angle.

questions.stem: An angle that is greater than 90° but less than 180° is called
questions.explanation: Obtuse angles lie between 90° and 180°.

questions.stem: What is the size of the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 3:00?
questions.explanation: Each hour mark is 30°, and from 12 to 3 is 3 x 30° = 90°.

questions.topic: Vertically opposite, adjacent, alternate and corresponding angles
questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles formed is 65°. What is the angle vertically opposite to it?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal.

questions.topic: Vertically opposite, adjacent, alternate and corresponding angles
questions.stem: A straight line cuts two parallel lines. One of the alternate angles is 3x and the other is 72°. Find x.
questions.explanation: Alternate angles are equal: 3x = 72°, so x = 24°.

questions.topic: Vertically opposite, adjacent, alternate and corresponding angles
questions.stem: A transversal cuts two parallel lines. If one of the co-interior (allied) angles is 108°, what is the other?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°: 180° - 108° = 72°.

questions.topic: Angles at a point and on a straight line
questions.stem: Four angles meet at a point. Three of them are 95°, 120° and 80°. Find the fourth angle.
questions.explanation: Angles at a point add to 360°: 360 - 295 = 65°.

questions.topic: Angles at a point and on a straight line
questions.stem: Angles 2x, 3x and 30° lie together on a straight line. Find x.

questions.topic: Sum of angles of a polygon
questions.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?

questions.topic: Sum of angles of a polygon
questions.stem: Find each interior angle of a regular octagon.
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°, so each interior angle is 180° - 45° = 135°.

questions.topic: Sum of angles of a polygon
questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: Number of sides = 360° ÷ 24° = 15.

questions.stem: A girl looks up from the ground at the top of a mast. The angle between her line of sight and the horizontal is called the angle of
questions.explanation: Looking up from the horizontal gives an angle of elevation.

questions.stem: From the top of a cliff, the angle of depression of a boat is 35°. What is the angle of elevation of the top of the cliff from the boat?
questions.explanation: The angle of depression from the cliff equals the angle of elevation from the boat (alternate angles).

questions.stem: A tree stands 40 m from a point on level ground. The angle of elevation of the top of the tree from the point is 30°. Find the height of the tree, correct to 1 decimal place. (tan 30° = 0.5774)
What is the three-figure bearing of a point due south-west of an observer?
questions.explanation: Measured clockwise from north: east is 090°, south is 180°, and south-west is 180° + 45° = 225°.

questions.stem: The bearing of town Q from town P is 070°. What is the bearing of P from Q?
questions.explanation: The back bearing differs by 180°: 070° + 180° = 250°.

questions.stem: Which three-figure bearing represents due east?
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, and east is a quarter turn: 090°.

questions.topic: Sine, cosine and tangent of an acute angle
questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite angle x is 3 cm and the hypotenuse is 5 cm. What is sin x?
questions.explanation: sin x = opposite ÷ hypotenuse = 3/5.

questions.topic: Sine, cosine and tangent of an acute angle
questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite angle y is 5 cm and the side adjacent to y is 12 cm. Find cos y.
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = square root of (25 + 144) = 13, so cos y = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 12/13.

questions.topic: Sine, cosine and tangent of an acute angle
questions.stem: Which ratio is defined as opposite side ÷ adjacent side?
questions.explanation: tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.

questions.stem: A ladder 10 m long leans against a wall and makes an angle of 40° with the ground. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall? (cos 40° = 0.7660)
questions.explanation: Distance = 10 x cos 40° = 10 x 0.7660 = 7.66 m.

questions.stem: Find the area of a triangle with base 14 cm and height 9 cm.
questions.explanation: Area = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x 14 x 9 = 63 cm^2.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 15 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. Find its area.
questions.explanation: Area = base x height = 15 x 8 = 120 cm^2.

questions.stem: How many square tiles of side 25 cm are needed to cover a floor 6 m by 4 m?
questions.explanation: Floor area = 24 m^2; each tile is 0.25 x 0.25 = 0.0625 m^2; 24 ÷ 0.0625 = 384 tiles.

questions.stem: A rectangular compound 20 m by 15 m has a path 1 m wide running round the inside edge. Find the area of the path.
questions.explanation: Inner rectangle = 18 m x 13 m = 234 m^2; path = 300 - 234 = 66 m^2.

questions.markingGuide:

2 marks: (a) Selling price = 30 x 1,200 = ₦36,000
2 marks: (b) Profit = ₦10,500

A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 7 m and a height of 20 m. (Take pi = 22/7)
(a) Find the area of the circular base of the tank. [3 marks]
(b) Find the volume of the tank in cubic metres (volume = base area x height). [4 marks]

questions.explanation: (a) Base area = 154 m^2. (b) Volume = 154 x 20 = 3,080 m^3. (c) Curved surface = 2 x 22/7 x 7 x 20 = 880 m^2. (d) Cost = 880 x 500 = ₦440,000.

questions.stem:
(a) A boy standing 25 m from the foot of a vertical flagpole on level ground observes the top of the pole at an angle of elevation of 23°. Using tan 23° = 0.4245, calculate the height of the flagpole, correct to 1 decimal place. [5 marks]
(b) A girl walks 12 km due east from village P to village Q, then 5 km due north to village R. (i) Calculate the distance PR. [4 marks] (ii) Calculate tan of angle RPQ and state the bearing of R from P, given that angle RPQ is about 23°. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) tan 23° = h/25 stated
3 marks: (a) h = 25 x 0.4245 = 10.6 m
2 marks: (b)(i) PR^2 = 12^2 + 5^2 = 169
2 marks: (b)(i) PR = 13 km
2 marks: (b)(ii) tan RPQ = 5/12
2 marks: (b)(ii) Bearing measured clockwise from north: 90° - 23° 
2 marks: (b)(ii) Bearing of R from P = 067°
questions.explanation: (a) h = 25 x tan 23° = 25 x 0.4245 = 10.6 m (1 d.p.). (b)(i) PR = square root of (144 + 25) = 13 km. (ii) tan RPQ = 5/12 (about 0.4167, so angle RPQ is about 23°). R is 23° north of east, so its bearing from P is 90° - 23° = 067°.

questions.stem:
At a school canteen, 2 meat pies and 3 bottles of water cost ₦1,300, while 3 meat pies and 2 bottles of water cost ₦1,450.
(a) Taking the cost of a meat pie as ₦x and a bottle of water as ₦y, write down two equations. [4 marks]
(b) Solve the equations to find the cost of a meat pie and of a bottle of water. [8 marks]
(c) How much would Tunde pay for 4 meat pies and 5 bottles of water? [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) 2x + 3y = 1,300
2 marks: (a) 3x + 2y = 1,450
4 marks: (b) Correct elimination or substitution method shown
2 marks: (b) x = 350 (meat pie ₦350)
2 marks: (b) y = 200 (water ₦200)
3 marks: (c) 4(350) + 5(200) = ₦2,400
questions.explanation: (a) 2x + 3y = 1,300 and 3x + 2y = 1,450. (b) Multiply the first by 3 and the second by 2: 6x + 9y = 3,900 and 6x + 4y = 2,900. Subtract: 5y = 1,000, so y = 200; then 2x = 1,300 - 600 = 700, so x = 350. (c) 1,400 + 1,000 = ₦2,400.

questions.stem:
The marks (out of 10) scored by 20 pupils in a quiz were:
4, 6, 5, 7, 6, 8, 6, 5, 9, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 8, 3, 6, 7, 5, 7
(a) Prepare a frequency table for the data. [5 marks]
(b) Find (i) the mode [2 marks] (ii) the median [3 marks] (iii) the mean mark. [4 marks]
(c) Find the range of the marks. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) Frequencies 3-1, 4-2, 5-4, 6-6, 7-4, 8-2, 9-1 (deduct 1 mark per error; total 20 shown)
2 marks: (b)(i) Mode = 6
3 marks: (b)(ii) 10th and 11th values are both 6, so median = 6
2 marks: (b)(iii) Sum of fx = 120
2 marks: (b)(iii) Mean = 120 ÷ 20 = 6
1 mark: (c) Range = 9 - 3 = 6
questions.explanation: (a) Mark 3: 1, 4: 2, 5: 4, 6: 6, 7: 4, 8: 2, 9: 1 (total 20). (b)(i) Mode = 6 (highest frequency). (ii) The 10th and 11th marks in order are both 6, so median = 6. (iii) Sum of fx = 3 + 8 + 20 + 36 + 28 + 16 + 9 = 120; mean = 120 ÷ 20 = 6. (c) Range = 9 - 3 = 6.

questions.stem:
In a survey, 60 JSS 3 pupils named their favourite fruit: orange 18, mango 15, banana 12, pawpaw 9 and pineapple 6.
(a) Calculate the angle of the sector for each fruit in a pie chart. [5 marks]
(b) State the steps you would follow to draw the pie chart. [3 marks]
(c) A pupil is chosen at random from the group. Find the probability that the pupil's favourite fruit is (i) mango [2 marks] (ii) not orange. [3 marks]
(d) What percentage of the pupils chose banana? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) Orange 108°, mango 90°, banana 72°, pawpaw 54°, pineapple 36° (1 mark each)
3 marks: (b) Draw a circle and a radius; measure each angle with a protractor from the previous line; label each sector
2 marks: (c)(i) 15/60 = 1/4
3 marks: (c)(ii) 1 - 18/60 = 42/60 = 7/10
2 marks: (d) 12/60 x 100 = 20%
questions.explanation: (a) Each pupil = 360 ÷ 60 = 6°: orange 108°, mango 90°, banana 72°, pawpaw 54°, pineapple 36° (total 360°). (b) Draw a circle, draw one radius, measure each angle in turn with a protractor, and label the sectors. (c)(i) 15/60 = 1/4. (ii) 42/60 = 7/10. (d) 20%.

(b) Draw the x- and y-axes with 2 cm to 1 unit, plot the points from the table and join them with a ruler, since the graph is a straight line. (c) 2x - 1 = 4 gives x = 2.5. (d) 2x > 6, so x > 3: draw an open circle at 3 and shade to the right.

questions.topic: Application of direct and inverse proportions
questions.stem:
(a) 18 labourers can weed a farm in 10 days. (i) How many days will 12 labourers take at the same rate? [4 marks] (ii) How many labourers are needed to finish the work in 6 days? [3 marks]
(b) A car uses 8 litres of fuel to travel 96 km. (i) How far can it travel on 30 litres? [3 marks] (ii) If fuel costs ₦1,050 per litre, find the cost of fuel for a journey of 240 km. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) 18 x 10 = 180 labourer-days
2 marks: (a)(i) 180 ÷ 12 = 15 days
3 marks: (a)(ii) 180 ÷ 6 = 30 labourers
3 marks: (b)(i) 96 ÷ 8 = 12 km per litre; 30 x 12 = 360 km
2 marks: (b)(ii) Fuel needed = 240 ÷ 12 = 20 litres
3 marks: (b)(ii) Cost = 20 x 1,050 = ₦21,000
questions.explanation: (a)(i) 180 labourer-days ÷ 12 = 15 days (inverse proportion). (ii) 180 ÷ 6 = 30 labourers. (b)(i) 12 km per litre, so 30 litres take it 360 km. (ii) 240 ÷ 12 = 20 litres; 20 x ₦1,050 = ₦21,000.
